'''Susuki Mizu Shrine''' (須須岐水神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in [[Chikuma City]], {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}. It is identified as the {{ill|Shikigesha|ja|式外社|simple|Shikigesha|zh|式外社|qid=Q118469772}} Susuki Mizu Shrine, with its {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ca|Classificació moderna dels santuaris xintoistes|es|Anexo:Santuarios sintoístas según el sistema moderno|fr|Système moderne de classement des sanctuaires shinto|ja|近代社格制度|simple|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|sv|Moderna systemet för rangordning av shinto-helgedomar|zh|近代社格制度|qid=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}} classification as a former {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}{{efn|District Shrines|WD=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha|1=modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/village shrine|qq=ja_comment|qid=Q134917316|qq= 近代社格制度|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q712534}}.

== Overview ==

According to shrine tradition, it was founded in the second year of the [[Hakuhō era]] (673 CE). Initially known as {{ill|Hōri Shrine|ja|祝神社}}, it later enshrined {{ill|Sannō Gongen|ja|山王権現|zh|山王權現|qid=Q11470054}} from {{ill|Hiyoshi Taisha|en|Hiyoshi Taisha|qid=Q656451|lt=Hiyoshi Taisha}} at the behest of {{ill|Kanasashi Toneri Masanaga|ja|金刺舎人正長}}, a {{ill|Gunji|ja|郡司|ru|Гундзи|uk|Ґундзі|zh|郡司|qid=Q4152149}} of {{ill|Hanishina District, Nagano|en|Hanishina District, Nagano|qid=Q726661|lt=Hanishina District}}, after flooding from the {{ill|Shinano River|ar|نهر شينانو|arz|نهر شينانو|ban|Tukad Shinano|be|Сінана|ca|Shinano|ceb|Shinano Gawa|cs|Šinano|de|Shinano (Fluss)|el|Σινάνο (ποταμός)|es|Río Shinano|eu|Shinano ibaia|fa|رود شینانو|fi|Shinanojoki|fr|Shinano-gawa|he|שינאנו|hi|शिनानो नदी|id|Sungai Shinano|it|Shinano (fiume)|ja|信濃川|ka|სინანო|ko|시나노강|lt|Šinanas|mk|Шинано (река)|mn|Шинаногава|ms|Sungai Shinano|my|ရှိနနိုမြစ်|nl|Shinano (rivier)|no|Shinano|pl|Shinano (rzeka)|pt|Rio Shinano|ru|Синано (река)|sh|Shinano|simple|Shinano River|sk|Šinano (rieka)|sr|Шинано|sv|Shinanogawa|th|แม่น้ำชินาโนะ|tr|Shinano Nehri|uk|Сінано (річка)|vi|Sông Shinano|zh|信濃川|qid=Q734455}} during the {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|qid=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan era}}. In later periods, it gained the patronage of the {{ill|Sanada clan|en|Sanada clan|qid=Q1002844|lt=Sanada clan}}, receiving land grants of 300 koku and festival contributions. 

Rebuilt in 1851 during the {{ill|Kaei|en|Kaei|qid=Q1146125|lt=Kaei era}} under the guidance of {{ill|Tatekawa Washirō Tomimasa|ja|立川和四郎富昌}}, the shrine was renamed from "Sannō Daigongen Palace" to "Susuki Mizu Shrine" by the {{ill|Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|lt=Yoshida family}} in 1781 ({{ill|Tenmei|de|Tenmei (Ära)|fa|تنمی|fr|Ère Tenmei|it|Tenmei|ja|天明|ko|덴메이|pt|Tenmei|ru|Тэммэй|simple|Tenmei|sr|Тенмеи|sv|Tenmei|th|เท็มเม|tr|Tenmei|zh|天明 (日本)|qid=Q1194121|lt=Tenmei}} 1). The shrine formerly held rituals involving the exchange of {{ill|Mikoshi|en|Mikoshi|qid=Q979940|lt=Mikoshi}} with {{ill|Amamiya Shrine|ja|雨宮の坐日吉神社}} but discontinued this in 1872 (Meiji 5).

The shrine grounds span approximately 27 ken (east to west) and 34 ken (north to south). Revered as a {{ill|Suijin|en|Suijin|qid=Q3137449|lt=water god}}, it has long served as the guardian deity of the Yashiro Irrigation Weir.

'''Susuki Mizu Shrine''' (須須岐水神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Chikuma, Nagano|ar|تشيكوما (ناغانو)|azb|چیکوما، ناقانو|ce|Тикума|ceb|Chikuma Shi|de|Chikuma (Nagano)|es|Chikuma (Nagano)|fa|چیکوما، ناگانو|fi|Chikuma (Nagano)|fr|Chikuma (Nagano)|gl|Chikuma|hy|Տիկումա|id|Chikuma, Nagano|it|Chikuma|ja|千曲市|ko|지쿠마시|mn|Чикүма|mzn|چیکوما، ناگانو|nl|Chikuma|pl|Chikuma (miasto)|pt|Chikuma|ro|Chikuma|ru|Тикума|sv|Chikuma|tg|Чикума|th|ชิกูมะ|tl|Chikuma, Nagano|tr|Chikuma, Nagano|tt|Тикума|uk|Тікума (Наґано)|ur|چیکوما، ناگانو|uz|Chikuma (Nagano)|vi|Chikuma, Nagano|war|Chikuma, Nagano|zh|千曲市|zh_classical|千曲市|zh_min_nan|Tikuma-chhī|zh_yue|千曲|qid=Q179757|lt=Chikuma, Nagano}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|en|Nagano Prefecture|qid=Q127877|lt=Nagano Prefecture}}, Japan. It is associated with the ancient {{ill|Shikigesha|ja|式外社|simple|Shikigesha|zh|式外社|qid=Q118469772}} Susuki Mizu Shrine and held the status of a village shrine (旧郷社) under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|ca|Classificació moderna dels santuaris xintoistes|es|Anexo:Santuarios sintoístas según el sistema moderno|fr|Système moderne de classement des sanctuaires shinto|ja|近代社格制度|simple|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|sv|Moderna systemet för rangordning av shinto-helgedomar|zh|近代社格制度|qid=Q712534|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines}}.

== Overview ==
According to shrine tradition, Susuki Mizu Shrine was founded in the second year of the {{ill|Hakuhō|ja|白鳳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hakuhō period|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11580612}} (673). Initially, it was known as the "Hōri Shrine" (祝神社), a name derived from the {{ill|Engishiki|ar|إنجيشيكي (كتاب ياباني)|de|Engishiki|es|Engishiki|fr|Engishiki|he|אנגישיקי|id|Engishiki|it|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|ko|엔기시키|min|Engishiki|mr|इंगिशिकी|nl|Engishiki|pt|Engishiki|ru|Энгисики|simple|Engishiki|tr|Engishiki|uk|Енґісікі|zh|延喜式|qid=Q1342448|lt=Engishiki}}. During the {{ill|Zhenguan|en|Zhenguan|qid=Q3577278|lt=Jōgan (era)}} era, following flooding of the {{ill|Shinano River|ar|نهر شينانو|arz|نهر شينانو|ban|Tukad Shinano|be|Сінана|ca|Shinano|ceb|Shinano Gawa|cs|Šinano|de|Shinano (Fluss)|el|Σινάνο (ποταμός)|es|Río Shinano|eu|Shinano ibaia|fa|رود شینانو|fi|Shinanojoki|fr|Shinano-gawa|he|שינאנו|hi|शिनानो नदी|id|Sungai Shinano|it|Shinano (fiume)|ja|信濃川|ka|სინანო|ko|시나노강|lt|Šinanas|mk|Шинано (река)|mn|Шинаногава|ms|Sungai Shinano|my|ရှိနနိုမြစ်|nl|Shinano (rivier)|no|Shinano|pl|Shinano (rzeka)|pt|Rio Shinano|ru|Синано (река)|sh|Shinano|simple|Shinano River|sk|Šinano (rieka)|sr|Шинано|sv|Shinanogawa|th|แม่น้ำชินาโนะ|tr|Shinano Nehri|uk|Сінано (річка)|vi|Sông Shinano|zh|信濃川|qid=Q734455}}, the regional governor of {{ill|Hanishina District, Nagano|en|Hanishina District, Nagano|qid=Q726661|lt=Hanishina District}}, {{ill|Kanasashi no Masanaga|ja|金刺正長}}, brought the {{ill|Sannō Gongen|ja|山王権現|zh|山王權現|qid=Q11470054}} from {{ill|Hiyoshi Taisha|en|Hiyoshi Taisha|qid=Q656451|lt=Hiyoshi Taisha}} and enshrined it alongside the main deity.

In the Edo period, the shrine received the patronage of the {{ill|Sanada clan|en|Sanada clan|qid=Q1002844|lt=Sanada clan}}, who donated 300 koku of land and additional resources for rituals. The shrine was reconstructed by {{ill|Tatekawa Washirō Tomimasa|ja|立川和四郎富昌}} in the fourth year of {{ill|Kaei|en|Kaei|qid=Q1146125|lt=Kaei}} (1851) following repeated flood damage. In the first year of {{ill|Tenmei|de|Tenmei (Ära)|fa|تنمی|fr|Ère Tenmei|it|Tenmei|ja|天明|ko|덴메이|pt|Tenmei|ru|Тэммэй|simple|Tenmei|sr|Тенмеи|sv|Tenmei|th|เท็มเม|tr|Tenmei|zh|天明 (日本)|qid=Q1194121|lt=Tenmei}} (1781), the shrine was renamed "Susuki Mizu Shrine" by the head of Shinto priests, the {{ill|Urabe clan|ja|卜部氏|en|draft:Yoshida family|lt=Yoshida clan}}.

Previously, the shrine participated in rituals involving the transfer of portable shrines (神輿) with {{ill|Amamiya Shrine|ja|雨宮の坐日吉神社}}, but these were discontinued in the fifth year of {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}} (1872).

The shrine site measures approximately 27 ken east-to-west and 34 ken north-to-south. It has been worshipped as a {{ill|Suijin|en|Suijin|qid=Q3137449|lt=water god}}, serving as the guardian of the Yashiro irrigation system.
